4.3.1.16.2 Efficient COM for large data
The rules for the decision whether to use Efficient COM for large data (LdCom) are
described in System Template [8], chapter 6.2.
[SWS_Rte_01376]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00246
⌈The RTE shall use LdCom for sending/receiving arrays of bytes if the corresponding
ISignal is mapped to LdComIPdu.⌋
Transmission
[SWS_Rte_01377]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00231
⌈The RTE shall use the LdCom_Transmit API if LdComApiType is set to LDCOM_IF
in LdComIPdu.⌋
In case If-API is used upon LdCom_Transmit, the transmit request is passed imme-
diately to the lower layer. After return of the API the data does not need to be locked.
[SWS_Rte_01378]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00231
⌈The RTE shall use the LdCom_Transmit API if LdComApiType is set to LDCOM_TP
in LdComIPdu.⌋
In case TP-API is used, after LdCom_Transmit one or more invocations of the re-
spective Rte_LdComCbkCopyTxData notification callback by LdCom will occur asyn-
chronously. The Transmission is finalized by the invocation of Rte_LdComCbkTpTx-
Confirmation notification callback as well.
During this time the data has to be available for being passed to LdCom.
[SWS_Rte_01379]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00246
⌈The RTE shall lock the signal buffer after it initiated a Tp Transmission (LdCom_-
Transmit returned E_OK).⌋
During the signal buffer is locked no further transmit requests are permitted on
that item. For data semantics this means that Rte_Write/Rte_Call will return
RTE_E_CO
